name: Mini squat
equipment: something to steady a hand on, optional
movement: standing, a quarter squat — the knees bent to about forty five degrees — and back up

phone.placement: Stand the phone up on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to you.

words.hint: Standing, a quarter squat — knees bent to about forty five degrees — and back up.
words.start: Stand the phone up on the floor. Stand side on to it, feet hip-width apart, arms out in front for balance.
words.position: Stand tall side on to the phone, feet hip-width apart and pointing forward, arms out in front or a hand on a chair back.
words.top: The knees bent to about forty five degrees — a quarter squat, no deeper — the hips back, the knees over the feet, the heels down and the chest up.
howto: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, toes forward, weight spread through the whole foot. Hold a chair if you need to.
Send the hips back and bend the knees to about forty five degrees — a quarter of the way down — knees in line with the second toes, heels on the floor, chest up.
Push through the whole foot to stand tall again. The rep counts there.
words.cannot: The knees collapsing inward and the weight shifting to one leg: it sees the knee bend from the side, the shin lean, the trunk and the heels. Keep the knees over the second toes yourself.
words.about: Mini squat — standing side on: the knee angle, 130–150° at the bottom (180 is straight; 135 is a quarter squat), and deeper than 130 is called — NHS leaflets for knee arthritis stop at about 45° of bend; a rep is under way under 165 and counts when the knee is back past 172; the knee no more than a tenth of a shin past the toe tips — knees over the toes are fine, well past them is a cue to sit back; the trunk no more than 35° forward; the heels down, read against the start. Hold two seconds at the bottom.
words.lost: Stand side on to the camera, the whole body in
words.early: Hold it at the top next time
words.safety: Shallow and slow. Stop if the knee sharpens or clicks painfully; a smaller bend is still an exercise.
words.easier: A smaller bend; a hand on a chair back; fewer reps.
words.harder: A deeper bend (within what the knee allows); a longer hold; a slow count down; a weight held at the chest.
words.mistakes: Going too deep; the knees travelling well past the toes; heels lifting; the chest falling forward; knees collapsing inward.

measurements.label: knee bend
measurements.why: The knee angle: 180 standing, 135 a quarter squat, 90 a full one. Also the progress measurement.

settings.label: Knee angle at the bottom, lowest (deepest allowed)
Knee angle at the bottom, highest (shallowest that counts)

measurements.label: knee past the toes

settings.label: Knee past the toe tips, at most (% of the shin)

measurements.why: How far the knee is ahead of the tips of the toes, as a share of the shin: 0 with the knee over the toe tips, + past them. Knees over the toes are fine; well past them the load moves onto the front of the knee, and sitting back a little takes it off.

measurements.label: trunk forward
measurements.why: The trunk off vertical, + forward: some lean is right; past 35 the chest is falling.

measurements.label: heel raised
measurements.why: The heel against the toe, as the change since the start: the heel coming off the floor as the knees go forward reads up. Read against the start, so the model's own slant of a flat foot is taken off.

settings.label: Heel lifted, at most (degrees from the start)

prompt.text: Sit back into a quarter squat

faults.label: Too deep
faults.text: Not so deep — a quarter bend is enough
faults.deep: Nearly a half squat — come up to a quarter bend

faults.label: Bend short
faults.text: Bend a little more, if it is comfortable

faults.label: Knees well forward
faults.text: Sit back a little — hips back, heels down
faults.deep: The knees are well past the toes — send the hips back
